Micrographia

Physiological descriptions of minute bodies made by magnifying glasses

Robert Hooke

Hooke's observations through the early microscope, from the point of a needle and the cells of cork to the eye of a fly and the flea.

docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The book of 1665 that showed the Royal Society, and then all Europe, the world under the microscope: sixty observations of needles, razors, silks, crystals, mould, cork (where Hooke named the "cells"), leaves, insects and lice, with his reflections on light, colour, combustion and fossils, and the moon and stars seen through the telescope.

From Wikisource · Public domain

Robert Hooke (1635–1703), Micrographia, London, for the Royal Society, 1665; text from Wikisource. This book is not stored in this library: each chapter is read from Wikisource when it is opened, shown in this library's format, and ends with its own attribution. Licence: Public domain.
